title: Africa's AI-native startups: where the funding sits and what is being built

claims.text: Nigerian startups raised $635 million between January and September 2026, according to data from Africa: The Big Deal.
claims.label: Nigeria

claims.text: Egypt raised $445 million in the same period, according to Africa: The Big Deal.
claims.label: Egypt

claims.text: Kenyan startups raised $201 million in the first nine months of 2026.
claims.label: Kenya

claims.text: South Africa raised $182 million in the same period, the least of the four largest markets.
claims.label: South Africa

claims.text: Nigeria, Egypt, Kenya and South Africa together took 85% of all country-specific startup funding, up from 83% in 2025.
In the first half of 2026, fintech was the largest funded sector at 41% ($556 million), ahead of logistics and transport at 35% ($472 million) and agriculture and food at 7% ($93 million).
Tanzania, Côte d’Ivoire and Morocco each attracted more than $25 million in the first half of 2026, as capital spread beyond the four largest markets.
UNESCO estimates that Africa is home to between 1,500 and 3,000 languages, according to a profile of Botlhale AI.
Botlhale AI, a South African startup, builds speech recognition and language tools for African languages, aimed at call centres.
Botlhale says up to 70% of calls in South Africa are in languages other than English.
The company says its models support 11 South African languages and it is expanding to Ghana, Kenya and Nigeria.
Amini, a Kenyan startup, uses satellite imagery and AI to map environmental and agricultural data, including soil, vegetation and carbon levels.
Aerobotics, a South African company, combines AI, drones and data analytics to help farmers monitor crop health.
Africa: The Big Deal is expected to publish a consolidated 2026 funding review before year-end, which will show whether Egypt's 27% share of first-half funding holds.
